name: Ad Placement Optimization
summary: No problem found; overlap and boundary checks match the original contest rules
effect: No effect on the scores of honest submissions.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the graded inputs are public, the score scale's reference points come from other contest inputs and were not checked, and available computing power can affect time-limited solvers.
technical_finding: No good-faith defect; graded cases are public seeds 0–49

name: Anchorhead Text Adventure
summary: No scoring problem; the grader counts each game's final score, not its peak
effect: No effect seen on any score. If 100 points cannot be reached in this game, the best possible score is 1 point lower.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the score is the final score of the best session, idle sessions close after 600 seconds, at most 3 sessions run at once, and full score was not shown.
technical_finding: Scores the final (not peak) score of the best session, divided by the game maximum; play is deterministic (Jericho seed 0); scoring confirmed on six full and partial native sessions

name: ANN Vector Search QPS
summary: No scoring problem found; measured speed depends on the machine
effect: No effect on the scores of honest submissions, but the same submission's speed varied by ±17% between runs, so scores from different machines are not comparable.

technical_finding: QPS host-dependent; scorer isolation out of scope

name: Apple Incremental Game
summary: No scoring problem found; the stated 1 GB memory limit is not enforced
effect: No effect on the scores of honest submissions. The memory note matters only to users who rely on the stated limit.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the 1 GB memory limit stated in the task text is not enforced by the grader for each solution.
technical_finding: Anchors consistent with an independent simulator; advertised 1 GB memory policy not enforced per solution (note)

name: Arc Compiler Runtime
summary: Hidden tests need an undocumented output format worth a third of the score
effect: Up to 33.67 points lost, without warning, by any solver who keeps the starter's format or does not guess the required message wording.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the instructions now describe the required return format, the three required message texts and the rules checked, and give the starter's real score. Grading is unchanged.
technical_finding: Hidden tests require an undocumented analyze() return format; TASK.md claims starter scores 0 (actual 35.59)

name: BipedalWalker Locomotion RL
summary: Scores are capped at 30 out of 100 by design, as the task states
effect: Every submission is limited to 30 of 100. A mismatched file scores like an untrained walker plus the points for loading.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: scores run from 0 to 30, not 0 to 100; 10 points come from loading checks; files with mismatched names or sizes load partly without an error.
technical_finding: Task score capped at 30 (disclosed design) → max normalized 30

name: Borden Source Inversion
summary: The hidden grading model uses unstated, non-physical conventions, so textbook solutions score near baseline
effect: About 24 points on the original grader's 0–109 scale, about 22 out of 100: the same honest fitting method scores 7.0 with a textbook model and 31.2 with the grader's hidden conventions. Affects every solver that follows the documentation.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: solvers receive the grader's own prediction code and an exact description of its conventions, and the score scale runs from 0 up to the true source's score of 109.
technical_finding: Hidden forward model uses an undisclosed non-physical convention (mass-rate as mass, no porosity, mg/m³ as mg/L, source plane at box bottom); honest textbook solver scores at baseline; raw score uncapped (109)
technical_max_effect: ≈24 points (7.0 vs 31.2 for the same honest fit)

name: Carleson Formalization
summary: No problem found; one placeholder definition accepts any value
effect: No effect measured. The unfinished definition affects one item and possibly later proofs; its effect on the score was not measured.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: one unfinished definition accepts any value, and the source project is incomplete, so some items may have no known proof.
technical_finding: Census: 0 targets unattainable, aux targets 5.0% and stable; a sorried data definition (C_LorentzInterpolation) admits any value; upstream project unfinished, so some targets may lack upstream proofs

name: College English Exam Bank
summary: Rubric rules the AI grader leaves out are counted as full marks
effect: Raises a score by up to the value of the left-out rules; an empty assessment scores 100. Any submission can be affected when the AI model's assessment is incomplete.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: an incomplete or self-contradicting assessment is requested again, and otherwise reported as a grading failure instead of full marks. Complete assessments score exactly as before.
technical_finding: Grader code treats an unassessed rubric rule as full marks
technical_max_effect: up to the omitted rules' value

name: Combinatorial Games Formalization
summary: No problem found; honest proofs in different styles earn the same credit
effect: No effect measured on the scores of honest submissions.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: about 25.1% of the credit comes from helper items Lean generates automatically; honest proofs in different styles earned the same credit in the test.
technical_finding: Shared Lean grader: native census shows honest term- and tactic-style proofs earn identical credit (16/3732); 0 targets unattainable; aux targets 25.1% of weight but stable

name: CTA Risk Budget Optimization
summary: The overseas-exposure limit check skips currency conversion, so dollar positions are undercounted
effect: Up to 5 points out of 100, only in the generous direction, and only for submissions holding US-dollar contracts. Compliant portfolios are never penalized.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: dollar positions are converted to yuan at that day's exchange rate before the 40% check. Portfolios in one currency score the same; breaching ones can lose up to 5 points.
technical_finding: Cross-border exposure omits USD→CNY conversion required by the risk policy (~7× undercount)

name: D-ABIC Gravity Inversion
summary: 42 points come from the submission's own unchecked self-reported results
effect: 42 points cannot be verified, for every submission. The form penalty costs up to about 46 points at a strong level, and 3.2 raw points at every level.
what_we_did: Removed: 42 points still come from unverified self-reported results. A partial fix removes the hidden form penalty, but that alone does not make the task usable.
technical_finding: 42 of the points come from self-reported JSON the judge cannot verify; an undisclosed data-space-only gate also penalised the model-space form the prompt allows (fixed in a partial v2)
technical_max_effect: 42 points unverifiable; form gate up to ~46 at strong tier

name: DCSS Dungeon AI
summary: Scoring matches the instructions; one failed game voids the whole submission
effect: No effect observed. In the worst case one failed game voids a whole submission; the effect of machine speed is unmeasured.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: one missing game record voids the score, scores depend on machine speed with unmeasured noise, and the top of the score scale has not been shown reachable.
technical_finding: One missing morgue voids the 5-game mean; wall-clock noise unmeasured

name: Equivalence Class Divide and Conquer
summary: One sub-problem's grader leaves the last step out of the cost limit check
effect: In the worst case a solution could gain up to 5.17 of 100 points. No real gain was shown.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the grader now counts the last step's cost too. Nothing else changes; the reference solution still scores 100.
technical_finding: T3 checker cost loop skips the final state (accepts ≤ limit + |last target|)
technical_max_effect: bounded (≤0.04% over limit); no gain shown

name: Exchange Core Throughput
summary: The correctness check misses wrong fees and lost messages, so broken engines get full credit
effect: Engines with these bugs get full credit instead of 0; in single runs one scored 24.4 versus 7.1 for the correct engine, a gap within speed noise.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: 33 of the project's own tests must pass before speed is measured, otherwise the score is 0. The missing build files are included, so grading works offline.
technical_finding: Correctness gate misses fee/event errors; incorrect engines score higher than correct one
technical_max_effect: full credit for an incorrect engine (two one-edit bugs passed the check; their higher raw scores in single runs are within throughput noise)

name: FFmpeg swscale Reimplementation
summary: Timed speed tests never check output, so failed calls earn speed credit
effect: Up to 18.93 points out of 100 shown for honest but unfinished submissions whose library fails or does nothing on a timed conversion.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: each timed call's result is checked, and failed or wrong output earns no speed credit. Correct submissions score as before, apart from timing noise.
technical_finding: Timed workloads never correctness-checked; failed calls earn speedup credit
technical_max_effect: up to ~19 points shown for honest-incomplete variants

name: FLT Regular Formalization
summary: No problem found; the 25 scored proofs match the task's own list
effect: No effect found on the scores of honest submissions.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the 25 weighted statements (total weight 87) match the task's list exactly, and none was found out of reach.
technical_finding: Census: 25 weighted targets (total weight 87) match the listing exactly; no aux targets; 0 unattainable

name: Git Rewrite in Zig
summary: No problem found; a correct program can earn the full 100
effect: No effect found for a correct program on an 8-core machine. Effects on machines with fewer cores were not measured.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: scoring uses git's own test suite, submissions must supply their own helper programs, and the per-script time limit was only tested on an 8-core machine.
technical_finding: Scoring path validated end-to-end with a real git positive control (29,075/29,075 tests, score 100); note: the prompt does not explain how scoring works, and the 120 s per-script timeouts were only tested on 8 cores

name: Graph Node Classification
summary: Non-numeric predictions are silently dropped and the run still counts as valid
effect: Only submissions with missing or non-numeric predictions are affected. It adds chance to their score; no expected gain was shown, and whether it can raise scores was not established.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: every test node must get a whole-number category, otherwise the run is marked invalid. Honest submissions score the same, apart from timing noise of about 0.008 points.
technical_finding: Non-integer predictions silently dropped and run marked valid; (NaN-confidence clipping is score-neutral)
technical_max_effect: variance only; no expected gain shown

name: Grid Turing Robot
summary: Scored correctly, but one failed case voids the whole submission unannounced
effect: About 20 points if one case fails; at most 2.84 points from the scale offset; up to the full score on graders with fewer than about 8 CPUs.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: one failed case voids the submission, a do-nothing solution scores 2.84 instead of 0, and repeatable results need at least 8 dedicated grader CPUs.
technical_finding: Baseline anchor 9,025,986 vs actual 7,744,909 (+2.84); one failed case voids submission (undisclosed); ≥8 CPUs needed for reproducibility
technical_max_effect: 2.84 (baseline anchor); ~20 if one case fails (undisclosed rule); up to full score on <8 judge CPUs

name: Integer Compression Codec
summary: Scores compare against stored numbers the documented starter cannot produce
effect: All submissions: the starter scores 0.24 instead of 1.0 and a simple honest codec 0.76 instead of 6.24; relative dataset weights are off by up to 6.7 times.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the grader measures the starter in the same run, as documented, and the 0–100 scale runs from the starter (0) to the formula's maximum (100). Scores are not comparable with the original version.
technical_finding: Stored baseline table (impossible <8 bpi for varint) replaces the documented starter baseline
technical_max_effect: starter 0.24 vs documented 1.0; honest codec 0.76 vs 6.24

name: Jagua Nesting Optimization
summary: The grader accepts overlapping shapes as valid layouts
effect: Layouts with overlaps can score above every valid layout. The size was not measured. Honest layouts without overlaps are unaffected.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the grader measures the exact overlap area between shapes and rejects any overlap larger than one millionth of the smaller shape's area, while edges that only touch stay allowed. It also rejects forbidden rotations.
technical_finding: Validator accepts large positive-area overlaps (identical placements, containment, half-slides)

name: Juliet Vulnerability Analyzer
summary: Answer key checks out; public and hidden examples differ in one convention
effect: About 2.5 points out of 100 (an estimate, not measured), only for solvers that copy the public command-injection convention. The use-after-free effect was not measured.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: hidden command-injection answers start at the input line, unlike the public examples; use-after-free answers start at the allocation, not the release; intermediate steps are not required.
technical_finding: Labels consistent (723/723); public/hidden CWE-78 trace convention differs

name: K-12 Math Recommendation
summary: No scoring problem found; shipped example reports are out of date
effect: No effect on honest submissions under normal memory limits. Under a tight memory limit every submission gets 0 with an error.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the shipped example reports are out of date, and the grader fails under a tight memory limit.
technical_finding: Reference solutions score validly (24.7 and 17.6) with enough memory; the scorer needs more than a 512 MiB address-space limit; the shipped evaluation_report.json files are stale against the current evaluator

name: Lean Analysis Proofs
summary: Two required statements are false; some points depend on proof style
effect: At least 49 of 2901 points (1.69%) are out of reach for any honest, complete solution; up to 466 points could depend on proof style.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the two false statements are corrected, and automatic helper entries and three placeholder statements are no longer scored, leaving 2338. Scores are not comparable with the original version.
technical_finding: Two required statements are false (refuted in Lean inside the task image), and compiler-generated auxiliary targets are credited by name and printed type, so at least 49 points (1.69%) are unattainable for any honest complete solution and up to 466 depend on proof style

name: Molecular Self Assembly
summary: The stated 1 GB memory limit is not enforced; no score advantage found
effect: No way found for extra memory to raise a score; this is reasoned, not measured. Solutions using too much memory may lose cases unpredictably.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: treat the 1 GB memory limit as advice only. Memory is limited only for the grader as a whole, which can fail memory-heavy solutions unpredictably.
technical_finding: Per-solution memory limit not enforced (one aggregate container limit)

name: NetHack Dungeon Agent
summary: Game seeding silently fails, so the 20 graded games are random and scores vary
effect: For the starter program, 0.02 points out of 100. The variation for a competent agent was not measured and is likely much larger.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the 20 games are random rather than fixed, scores are not repeatable between runs, and each game is limited to 5,000 steps and 120 seconds, the latter not stated.
technical_finding: Seeding silently fails: the 20 graded games are unseeded and random (run-to-run variance unmeasured for scoring agents); 120 s per-game limit not stated in the prompt

name: New Foundations Consistency
summary: Grades correctly with internet access; cannot grade offline
effect: No effect measured. Offline graders give no score at all. The renaming risk is at most 0.67% of the score, an upper bound, not a measured loss.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: grading needs internet access to GitHub, and 15 automatically generated items (at most 0.67% of the score) could be lost when honest proofs rename them.
technical_finding: Grades correctly with the judge's network (Lake re-clones doc-gen4 at the manifest-pinned commit 86d735ec, valid result); cannot be graded offline; 15 of 370 aux targets exposed to renumbering (≤0.67%), untested

name: OpenRCT2 Theme Park AI
summary: Instructions promise about 4 game years; the grader runs about 68 game days
effect: Not measured as a score change. It changes what is measured: company value after about 2 months, not 4 years, for solvers who planned for the stated length.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the instructions now state the real 120-second limit, about 70 game days at speed 4, and that the plugin may set speed 1 to 4. Grading is unchanged.
technical_finding: Promised ~4 game years cannot run in the 120 s budget (~68 game days observed); score is an early snapshot

name: OpenTTD Transport AI
summary: The instructions name a game function that does not exist
effect: Up to the whole score for a submission that follows the instructions and calls the missing function. Submissions that use a different function are not affected.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the instructions and starter program name the correct function and explain how the score is read. The grader is unchanged, so each submission scores the same.
technical_finding: Prompt goal names a non-existent API (AICompany.GetCompanyValue); a script that calls it dies, and the shipped baseline dies on its first statement; scorer itself works
technical_max_effect: whole score for prompt-following solvers (script dies at the call; score is 0 or an earlier quarter's value)

name: Order Addition Permutation Optimization
summary: An outdated file check fails every submission, so later improvements are ignored
effect: Each submission's own score is unaffected. A run's reported best score is wrong whenever a later valid submission scores higher; how often this happened was not measured.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the check uses the current file's fingerprint, so correct submissions pass all five tests and the best submission, not the first, is chosen.
technical_finding: Integrity test expects a stale helper hash; every submission capped at pass rate 0.8, so pass_rate_first freezes the run on its first valid submission

name: Ordinal Notation Well-Foundedness
summary: Grader correct; only the first of nine targets is known to be provable
effect: No effect on honest proofs was found. A proof needing a helper file with an excluded name, or taking over 300 seconds to compile, would fail.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: targets 2 to 9 are unproven, helper files with certain name prefixes are dropped, and each file has a 300-second compile limit.
technical_finding: Grader correct on honest/Admitted/axiom controls; helper file-name filter undisclosed; targets 2–9 unproven

name: PFR Formalization
summary: No problem found; two proof styles scored the same
effect: No effect found on the scores of honest submissions.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: two proof styles scored the same, no statement was found out of reach, and five statements that display as unfinished are not actually unfinished.
technical_finding: Census: honest proofs in two styles score identically (2/423); 0 unattainable; 5 autoParam types print as sorry but are not holes

name: Portfolio Risk Calibration
summary: Excess return uses a slightly different formula than the instructions state
effect: The total score moves by at most about 0.4 of 100 points, for all submissions. The ranking of excess returns does not change.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the grader's excess-return formula differs from the stated one, moving totals by at most about 0.4 points; a two-line fix exists if exact agreement is needed.
technical_finding: Annual excess computed as annualized difference, not difference of annualized returns

name: Rust Multicrate Reconstruction
summary: A test exemption can forgive one unrelated failure, worth at most 0.1 points
effect: At most +0.1 points out of 100 per grading, only for solvers whose excused test passes while another test in the same package fails.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: scores may be overstated by at most 0.1 points out of 100, because one unrelated failure can be credited as a pass; a one-condition fix is described.
technical_finding: Exempt-test credit can forgive an unrelated failure

name: Schemathesis Config Modernization
summary: One test does not check that a function is returned unchanged
effect: At most about 1/150 of the total score, only for submissions whose decorator returns something other than the original function.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: one test is added that checks the function comes back unchanged. Scores are identical when that test group is fully passed or fully failed.
technical_finding: Phase 3 test checks callable() not identity

name: Schemathesis Datagen Pipeline
summary: The date test checks only the format, not whether dates are real
effect: At most about 1% of the total score, only for generators that produce invalid dates or times; they get the same credit as correct generators.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the test now checks real calendar dates, matching weekdays and valid times, and samples 200 dates instead of 50. Correct generators keep their scores; wrong ones lose about 1%.
technical_finding: HTTP-date check is shape-only (accepts invalid dates/times)

name: Schemathesis Reporting Observability
summary: Two hidden tests give credit for wrong or broken output
effect: About 2.4% of the total in all: at most 1/70 (about 1.4%) and 1/100 (1.0%). Only submissions with these mistakes gain.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the report test reads the file and requires the recorded error; the other test now checks real output. Partial scores are not comparable with the original version.
technical_finding: JUnit check accepts malformed output; body-coverage test is vacuous

name: SMT Solver
summary: The answer checker misreads some valid solutions, so 27 hidden problems cannot be won
effect: A perfect solver's maximum falls from 78.61 to 72.40 (6.21 points). All solvers lose the 27 problems; those following the documented format also lose 42 more.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the checker works out a function's actual inputs before looking up its value, so correct answers in the documented format are accepted; wrong answers are still rejected.
technical_finding: Witness checker keys UF values by source text, so 27 satisfiable hidden files are unwinnable

name: Sphere Eversion Formalization
summary: No problem found; all scored items reachable by an honest solution
effect: No effect measured.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the finding that automatically generated items are stable rests on inspection only; no honest proof was scored.
technical_finding: Census: 0 targets unattainable; aux targets 18.0% and stable (controls only, no honest-proof test)

name: Treant Forest
summary: The score scale tops out at 21 of 100 for any submission
effect: Every submission's score is squeezed into 0 to 21, with ordering kept. A simple honest test submission scored 3.04.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: only the score scale changes, running straight from the starter's total (3,418) to the maximum possible (92,304). Raw totals are identical; the simple honest test submission now scores 16.36.
technical_finding: Anchors exceed the 2N² turn cap: max normalized 21.02; movement semantics question separate

name: Tree Block Partitioning
summary: The supplied grading library miscalculates when a value multiplies itself
effect: At most 5 of 100 points, only for submissions that multiply a value by itself. The other 95 points are unaffected.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: two lines in the grader's library swap order so both old values are read first. The reference solution still scores 100.
technical_finding: Supplied in-place multiply wrong when operands alias (v *= v)

name: Triangulation Coloring Optimization
summary: The grader allows mesh moves the instructions forbid, and its test inputs overlap
effect: Changes which moves are allowed for every solver. How much a strong solver gains from forbidden moves was not measured.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: forbidden swaps are rejected and the test inputs are rebuilt without overlaps. Scores are not comparable with the original version.
technical_finding: Flip-legality rule omits the README's convexity condition; the same rule generated the cases (all 10 overlap/fold) and scores submissions
technical_max_effect: material: changes which flips are legal for every solver

name: Trinity Text Adventure
summary: No problem found; the score is the game's own, and play is repeatable
effect: No effect on the scores of honest submissions observed. Only an agent that relies on the highest-score-reached figure, or pauses over 10 minutes mid-game, could be affected.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the final score of the best session counts, idle sessions close after 600 seconds, and at most 3 sessions run at once.
technical_finding: Scores the final (not peak) score of the best session, divided by the game maximum; play is deterministic (Jericho seed 0); scoring confirmed on six full and partial native sessions

name: Tryst Text Adventure
summary: No problem found; the score is the game's own repeatable score
effect: No effect observed. Only an agent relying on the peak score, or pausing over 10 minutes mid-game, could be affected.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the score is the final in-game score of the best session, out of 350, and sessions close after 600 seconds idle, with at most 3 at once.
technical_finding: Scores the final (not peak) score of the best session, divided by the game maximum; play is deterministic (Jericho seed 0); scoring confirmed on six full and partial native sessions

name: Vehicle Routing Time Windows
summary: No scoring problem; the checker is built from a file solvers may edit
effect: None for a program that reports its own computed cost. Editing the shared distance file was not tested, so any effect is not measured.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: editing the shared distance file also changes the checker; all 56 public cases count equally; report the computed cost exactly. Building the checker from the original file is recommended.
technical_finding: Decimal tolerance immaterial (exact check); instruction clarification adopted as note; the verifier is compiled from the submitted include/types.h, so a solver edit to the distance code changes the checker (recommended hardening: build verifier from the original header)

name: Vibrating Path Graph Coloring
summary: The tester rejects one documented output format, but no score changes
effect: No effect on any score on the official puzzles; a solver using the documented no-hit format only sees a different error message.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the tester accepts no-hit answers only in two lines, not the documented three, but a no-hit answer is wrong on every official puzzle, so no score changes.
technical_finding: Tester rejects documented 3-line zero-hit format

name: VLIW Kernel Optimization
summary: No problem found for honest submissions
effect: No effect on the scores of honest submissions.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: this audit does not cover deliberate attempts to cheat the grader; the two test submissions run were scored correctly.
technical_finding: Only scorer-isolation issues (out of scope)

name: Warehouse Forklift Routing
summary: Time limit is stricter than promised, and no score can exceed about 30
effect: A solver taking 60 to 150 seconds on any input loses its whole score; every solver is capped at about 30.3 out of 100.
what_we_did: Fixed in a new version: the time limit is 150 seconds per input, as promised. The score scale is unchanged, and the ceiling of about 30.3 is documented.
technical_finding: Prompt promises 30 s per test case (150 s/input) but the evaluator gives 60 s per input; and a lower bound proved in Lean for a model of the tester (model matched to the tester by a 294-string differential test) shows every valid TOTAL ≥ 712.538 > rank1 395.80, so the top two anchors are unreachable and normalized scores are capped at ≈30.3
technical_max_effect: whole score for budget-following solvers; ~70 points of the scale unreachable

name: Wesnoth Tactical AI
summary: The supplied starter program is broken, and repeat games give different results
effect: The broken starter scores 0 for anyone who submits or builds on it unchanged. The effect of non-repeatable games on scores was not measured.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: the starter's recruiting setting is broken on this game version, games are not repeatable, and 60 games must fit in 900 seconds.
technical_finding: Evaluation fits budget (80–172 s); shipped baseline recruit config broken (scores 0); games not repeatable

name: Wireless Electricity Layout
summary: A program that fails to compile can be listed as best, but scores never change
effect: No effect on scores out of 100: every affected submission scores 0 either way, an argument checked on 200,000 random submission histories.
what_we_did: Kept, with a note: a compile failure is penalized once rather than per test case, so it can be named the best submission, but this never changes a score out of 100.
technical_finding: Compile failure counted once vs per case in raw totals
technical_max_effect: 0 normalized (monotonicity argument, checked on 200,000 random histories)
